objective: Establish a reproducible TypeScript repository, architecture boundaries, versioned IR schemas, development tooling, ADRs, fixture/test skeletons, and a Gate 1 plan without implementing Gate 1 behavior.
inScope: npm workspaces and TypeScript project references
format, lint, typecheck, test, build, and clean commands
schemas, core, and Spine adapter-boundary packages
AssetSpec, MeshSpec, RigSpec, WeightSpec, ConstraintSpec, AnimationSpec, BuildManifest, and ValidationReport
repository documentation, ADR-001 through ADR-006, fixture placeholders, and Gate 1 plan
runtime schema contract tests and package-boundary tests
outOfScope: Spine compiler or Spine JSON implementation
asset parsing, mesh generation, rig solving, weight solving, constraint solving, and animation generation
AI, MCP, Skill, preview renderer, GUI, and production CLI
changedFiles: README.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, ROADMAP.md, ASSUMPTIONS.md, and BACKLOG.md
assumptions: Node.js 22.12+ and npm workspaces are the initial supported toolchain.
TypeBox 0.x LTS is the source for runtime JSON-schema-compatible contracts and inferred types.
IR schema version 0.1 is pre-MVP and changes require an explicit migration and ADR.
Gate 0 validates document shape; semantic validators are owned by later Gates.
Exact Spine 4.3 format details remain unverified until Gate 1 research.
A production CLI starts with the first real command surface rather than a Gate 0 no-op command.
implementationSummary: The repository now has a deliberately small npm workspace. Schemas owns eight versioned runtime contracts and inferred TypeScript types. Core only re-exports engine-neutral contracts. The Spine package declares the 4.3 compatibility target but contains no compiler. Documentation fixes dependency direction, deterministic execution, AI boundaries, CLI-first delivery, and the Gate 1 research-first plan.

checks.name: clean install
checks.evidence: 134 packages installed; npm audit reported 0 vulnerabilities.

checks.name: full verification
checks.evidence: Prettier, ESLint, TypeScript project build/typecheck, and Vitest all passed.

checks.name: contract tests
checks.evidence: 2 test files and 13 tests passed, covering all eight schemas, rejection behavior, serialization/IDs, package facade, Spine target, and absence of compiler export.

checks.name: deterministic build evidence
checks.evidence: 52 emitted files, excluding incremental metadata, had byte-identical SHA-256 hashes across two clean builds.

compatibilityEvidence: Spine 4.3 is recorded only as a target boundary; Gate 0 makes no claim that a compiler or serialized document is compatible.
Gate 1 requires official documentation/runtime evidence, a real editor export, a golden test, and CLI verification before accepting format behavior.
knownLimitations: Fixture directories contain explicit README placeholders only because no engine behavior exists to generate honest artifacts in Gate 0.
Schemas enforce structural constraints but intentionally do not claim topology, hierarchy, weight-sum, or loop semantics.
There is no production CLI because Gate 0 has no real executable engine operation.
Spine coordinate, angle, omission, default-value, and patch-version conventions remain open Gate 1 questions.
risks: IR schema 0.1 may need migration after a verified Spine export clarifies coordinate or attachment requirements.
A future Gate could accidentally leak target-specific fields into Core; ADRs and package-boundary tests are the current guardrails.
